To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the closed-form solutions for displacements are derived for the exponentially increasing shear modulus and the seismic amplification characteristics for the sites with exponentially increasing shear moduli are discussed.

the seismic amplification of the sites with exponentially increasing shear moduli with depth is a function of the characteristics of the site,the frequency of the excitation, the impedance ratio of bedrock and the soil layer and the predominant period of the site.

the predominant period of a soil layer with an exponentially increasing shear modulus is four times the total shear-wave travel time through the soil layer, and that the predominant period is a good estimate of the period at which the seismic amplification of the layer is maximum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the theory for the analysis of sites on bedrock with an exponentially increasing shear modulus.
the development of a new method of analysis of seismic wave propagation and amplification in a soil layer on a bedrock.

the study of the seismic response of sites with exponentially increasing shear moduli with depth.The closed-form analytical solution for the displacements is developed for the case of a single layer on a half-space.The study of an illustrative example shows that the site characteristics and the vibration frequency affect the seismic amplifications.The predominant period of the layer is proved to be a useful estimate for the nonlinear sites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the amplification of the shear seismic waves at the surface is dependent on the frequency and the impedance contrast of the bedrock and the half-space.The amplification is a maximum at the fundamental frequency and decreases with increasing frequency.
the present study has provided a useful tool for the analysis of the seismic amplifications of sites with exponentially increasing shear moduli with depth.

the seismic amplification at the surface of a site with exponentially increasing shear wave modulus with depth is a function of the site characteristics, the vibration frequency, and the impedance ratio between the half-space and soil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the closed-form analytical solution of the one-dimensional site response is very helpful in understanding the mechanism of seismic amplification of the sites with exponentially increasing shear wave velocity with depth.

for the sites with exponential shear modulus with depth,the predominant period of a site is four times the total shear-wave travel time through the soil layer,which is a good estimate for the site period.The seismic amplification is affected by the site characteristics,the vibration frequency and also the impedance ratio between the bottom surface of soil layer and the half-space.

the closed-form solution of the seismic displacement is a good tool in the analysis of sites subjected to vertically propagating shear waves and the predominant period of the site is a good estimate of the predominant period of seismic waves in the site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the seismic amplification of sites can be studied by the analytical solutions for exponentially increasing shear modulus.
the seismic amplification can be predicted by the closed-form analytical solution for the single layer with exponentially varying shear modulus with depth.
the closed-form solutions for displacements in the soil layer and the bedrock are very helpful in understanding the seismic response of sites.
